Center.looks: Fails clustered in a disc around the wafer centre.
causes: Abnormal liquid flow or liquid pressure

Donut.looks: A ring of fails part-way out, with a cleaner centre and edge.
causes: At one technology node: under-etched metal causing resistive vias in the ring

Edge-Loc.looks: A cluster of fails at one spot on the edge.

Edge-Ring.looks: Fails all the way around the outer edge.
causes: At one technology node: poly critical dimension (CD) running short near the edge

Loc.looks: One local cluster of fails away from the edge.

Random.looks: Fails scattered across the wafer with no cluster.
causes: Particles such as dust scattered over the surface

Scratch.looks: A thin line or arc of fails.
causes: Sharp edges touching and slipping on the wafer surface during manufacturing or wafer test

none.looks: No defect pattern: only a few scattered fails.

geng2023.text: Geng, Sun, Chen, Xu, Ho and Yu, 'Mixed-Type Wafer Failure Pattern Recognition' (invited paper), ASP-DAC 2023

hu2021.text: Hu, He and Li, 'Semi-supervised Wafer Map Pattern Recognition using Domain-Specific Data Augmentation and Contrastive Learning', IEEE International Test Conference 2021

wu2015.text: Wu, Jang and Chen, 'Wafer Map Failure Pattern Recognition and Similarity Ranking for Large-Scale Data Sets', IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing 28, 2015 (WM-811K)

audit.rule: >= 8 of 10 nearest other-lot wafers agree on a different label and the ensemble gives it >= 0.8
audit.note: Dropping suspects favours the model (it agrees with their suggested label), so the second F1 is an upper bound, not a corrected score.
